audit: A run's window was the next 24 overpasses counting the hidden ones, and each prediction was made at the hidden overpass's own time and pixel size, so the hidden rows moved the window, the estimate, the belief frames and the exports. The second baseline's pixel ratio in validation came from a calendar that still held the three test fires. Windows, start dates and episodes were chosen counting hidden overpasses, so removing the hidden instrument moved them. In the next-look environment the decisions were the hidden overpasses themselves and a pixel size was taken over the whole hidden pass, so rows an agent had not been shown changed what it saw and how many turns it had. 49 rows of 2021 inside the test boxes (32 in Dixie's, 9 in Lytton Creek's, 8 in northern Evia's) lay outside the fires' own dates and stayed in the baseline's training rows. None of this carried the hidden fire's position or power into the estimate, but each path let the hidden instrument shape the test. The project's own leak tests missed it: they changed hidden values and never deleted a row. The corrected protocol seals the hidden rows away until scoring.

fitted_values.note: Fitted and validated under the same protocol

validation.decision: fitted values are used: on validation fires they are ahead of both baselines on 2 of 7 scores, tied on 5 and behind on none, beyond the noise of resampling the fires
validation.rule: validation fires are resampled whole (2,000 times); a score is ahead when the 90 percent interval of its improvement over each baseline is above zero, behind when it is below zero against one of them, a tie otherwise. The fitted values are used when no score is behind and at least one is ahead. A part is on when every score of the part is ahead (and, for FRP, the 90 percent interval held for at least 80 percent of validation overpasses); otherwise the part is experimental.

empty_looks.what: scored looks at which the hidden instrument flagged no pixel in the box; cloud is not known

intervals.rule: the interval a prediction states is the prediction times two multiples, taken from the ratios of hidden over predicted on the training looks, every look with a positive prediction counted and a look that flagged nothing counted with a ratio of zero. Two-sided, the multiples are the 5th and the 95th percentile and hold 90 percent between them. When the 5th percentile is zero, which happens as soon as more than one training look in twenty flagged nothing, nothing is cut off below, and the 95th percentile would hold 95 percent: the interval is then one-sided, from zero to the 90th percentile. It starts at zero because cloud is not known, and an interval that could not hold an empty pass would claim more than the record supports.

before.note: the interval the values held until it was set again: the 5th and the 95th percentile of the training ratios. Its lower end was zero, so it held what lies below the 95th percentile, about 95 percent, while stating 90. The three recorded looks at the test fires were taken with it and state it; they are not scored again

limits: A pass that flagged nothing is scored as a look that flagged nothing: 6 of 153 validation looks. Cloud is not known, so such a pass may have been cloudy rather than free of fire, and the stated FRP interval starts at zero for that reason.

Validation rests on 7 episodes of 2024 and 2025 from 2 of the three regions (northern Evia's region has none). No part of the estimate is switched on there: 2 of 7 scores are ahead of both baselines, 5 are tied and 0 are behind, judged with an interval.
A pass whose swath held only part of the box is not scored: 1 on northern Evia (133 hidden pixels).
northern Evia is the weakest of the three: ahead of both baselines on 3 scores of 7 by plain comparison.
FIRMS lists detections, not where a satellite looked and saw nothing, and has no cloud mask: a revealed tile with no detection may have been cloudy rather than free of fire.

protocol.what: A test of the estimate made from MODIS alone, with VIIRS hidden, on fires it has never been fitted, validated or tested on, chosen by rule across the world. Two looks, each taken once: test A with the values in use, and test B after a refit on a fitting set and its validation. Each is recorded beside the three looks at the 2021 test fires under its own name, and reported as it is.
protocol.store: Rows come from FIRMS's yearly country files in the shared store, every country READY.md lists when the plan is made. The plan waits for the store to hold every country; if the lead calls it earlier, it runs on the countries listed, and the record names every country left out. Rows of FIRMS types 1, 2 and 3 (volcano, static land source, offshore) are left out of both instruments, as the Record counts a box.
protocol.places: A place is a square of 2.5 degrees on a grid from 180 W and 90 S, cut into 25 tiles of 0.5 degrees, as a region's context box is cut into its 25 test boxes. A place that meets the context box of plumas_ca, lytton_bc or evia_greece, edges touching included, is not in the test, in any year, so no row near a closed test fire is touched. Each place has a continent and a zone, both from the coordinates of its centre (continent_of, zone_of). The zone, from latitude, stands in for fuel: no map of fuel is read, and the record says so.
protocol.split: By place, from coordinates alone. Places are grouped in blocks of 10 degrees; a block's role is the share its sha256 falls in, of six equal shares: three for fitting, one for validation, one for test A and one for test B (role_of_block). A place of validation, test A or test B that meets a place of another role, corners included, is left out, so no place of those three roles is next to a place of any other role. No row of either instrument is read to split.
protocol.offered_regions: A place of validation, test A or test B that meets the context box of a region the page offers, edges touching included, is left out of its role in every year, so that the page cannot show a row of a test before its look; fitting places are not touched. The regions offered are every region the registry of places holds when the plan is made and every region the data side has named for the page by then, each by its context box, read from coordinates alone. The plan's record names each region with its box, and how many places the rule costs each role, continent and zone (offered_cost).
protocol.episodes: By the rule in use (backend/model/episodes.py, find_episodes, with its defaults), each place standing for a region's context box: in each tile and year from 2018 to 2022, the run of 12 consecutive MODIS overpasses that flagged the most MODIS pixels in the tile, kept when it flagged at least 60 and spans at most 120 hours; at most the three busiest tiles a place and year. VIIRS rows are never opened to choose. Then, per place, the busiest episode of each year by MODIS pixels in its tile, and of those the two busiest. Then, per role and continent, up to the quota (50 for fitting, 20 for validation, 20 for test A, 20 for test B), taken round the zones in the order tropical, subtropical, temperate, boreal, the busiest left in a zone at each turn; a zone with none left is passed over. Ties go to the earlier window, then to the place further west and south. A continent with fewer episodes than its quota gives what it has, and no other continent makes up the difference.
protocol.after_the_plan: The plan (every place with its role, continent and zone, every episode chosen, the MODIS files read with their sha256) is committed before any VIIRS file is opened for the test. Then the rows of both instruments inside each chosen place over its window and two days either side are read; the pass lists of the hidden platforms are fetched from NASA CMR for each window; and the monthly counts the second baseline needs are taken. An episode whose pass list cannot be fetched, or whose rows cannot be read, is listed as not scored, with the reason; nothing takes its place.
protocol.scored: Protocol version 3 of the blind test, VIIRS hidden: one prediction per pass of a hidden platform in NASA's pass list whose swath held the whole tile, each scored whether or not it flagged anything; never the nominal schedule. The estimate and the two baselines as they are: painted_modis, and overlap_ratio with the frozen power ratio and, for its pixel count, the place's own calendar ratio by the Record's rule (Suomi NPP rows over Terra and Aqua rows across the clean overlap months of the place, the years of the run left out; calendar_ratio). The seven scores of verdict, and beside them the share of looks whose hidden total power lies inside the stated interval.
protocol.counted: Both ways, each saying its kind. Per fire, a plain comparison: the scores on which the estimate is strictly better than both baselines on that episode. Per continent, per zone and over all, judged with an interval: the episodes are resampled whole 2,000 times (bootstrap_verdict, seed and level as in use), and a score is ahead, tied or behind. A set of few episodes has a wide interval, and the record gives each set's size.
protocol.test_a: One look at the test A episodes with the values in use, frozen by their sha256 in FROZEN_VALUES, after the rows and pass lists are in and before the refit starts. Nothing of the refit or its decision reads a test A result.
protocol.refit: The search of backend/model/fit_real.py as it is (its grid, objective, matching of counts and interval rule), started from the priors, on the fitting set: the fitting episodes of the plan and the 17 open training episodes of the three first regions (2018, 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2023). Then the refit and the values in use are both run on the validation episodes of the plan.
protocol.decision: The refit is the one test B is looked at with when, on the validation episodes, judged with an interval: (1) the rule in use for fitted values holds for it, no score behind either baseline and at least one ahead of both (fit_real.decide); and (2) against the values in use, no score is behind. Otherwise test B is looked at with the values in use and the refit is kept on record, unused. The decision is committed before test B is looked at.
protocol.test_b: One look at the test B episodes with the values the decision chose. Nothing has read a test B row of VIIRS before it, apart from the second baseline's monthly counts of other years.
protocol.test_b_methods: Test B's headline is the values the decision chose. Beside it, in the same look and on the same looks, test B also scores the other of the two values (the refit or the values in use) and every challenger model handed over before the look (backend/model/challenger, each a Method of the blind test) whose code was checked against these rules first: fitted on the fitting episodes and chosen on the validation episodes only, shown no row of test A or test B before the look. Each is judged against the two baselines by the same counts, and against the headline with an interval. None of them takes the headline's place, and nothing is chosen from what they show.
protocol.clear_looks: A second table, beside the main one and never in its place. If the share of each hidden pass's tile under cloud, by that pass's own cloud mask (the shared store's passmask), is on hand when a look is taken, the look also scores the same episodes on the looks whose hidden pass put at most a quarter of the tile under cloud, through the blind test's target filter, counted both ways. The masks are read for scoring only; no method is given any of them. A look taken without the masks has no second table and says so, and a look whose masks hold no share for a pass leaves that pass out of the second table.
protocol.players: The players of the round (backend/env) under the reward in use, on the same split: anything a player learns is fitted on the fitting episodes and chosen on the validation episodes, and the players are measured once on the test B episodes, after test B's look.
protocol.never: Nothing is fitted, chosen or switched because of a test A or test B result, and neither look is taken again. A result behind in a continent or a zone stays in the record as it is.

sources.reports_note: the reports are the files the runs on the three test fires wrote. They are not in the repository: the record holds what the sheet needs of each, and each report's sha256, so that whoever holds the reports can check the record against them. Each is named by its folder (report_folders says what a folder holds) and its file

report_folders.first-reconstruction: untuned priors on the windows of look 1, and Dixie with one VIIRS platform hidden
report_folders.first-fit: look 1: the first fitted values, under protocol version 1
report_folders.terra-morning: the other direction: Terra's morning pass estimated from VIIRS
report_folders.other-windows: runs with VIIRS hidden from other start dates, under protocol version 1
report_folders.sealed-protocol: look 2 and the runs from each default start, under protocol version 2; and what the schedule costs, on training fires
report_folders.sealed-protocol-scheduled-frames: the same runs with scheduled looks among the frames, a variant that was not adopted
report_folders.final-look: look 3, the final look, under protocol version 3

count_kinds.plain comparison: a score counts as ahead when it is strictly better than every baseline's on the looks scored, with no allowance for noise; the count of one fire or one run, where there is nothing to resample
count_kinds.judged with an interval: the fires are resampled whole; a score is ahead when the interval of its improvement over each baseline lies above zero, behind when it lies below zero against one of them, and tied otherwise; the count over a set of fires
